Subject: EU/APAC local SI engagement & data residency plan

Hi all,

Following up from last week's partner forum — I want to align on a short roadmap for engaging local system integrators in EU and APAC with a focus on data residency and deployment models (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). Key goals:

- Validate which SIs have experience with data‑sovereignty requirements (GDPR, regional cloud providers, on‑prem installs).
- Capture the minimal evidence bundle we need to share (SOC2, DFDs, KMS options, sample contracts).
- Define a pilot engagement for one EU SI (ClearSky) and one APAC SI (Toshi Systems).

Attachments: regional-partner-matrix.xlsx (draft) — matrix includes country coverage, cloud partners, legal constraints.

Asks:
1) Sergio/Hannah — can you review the matrix and flag any gaps on technical support or billing flows?
2) Karthik/Kim — legal/compliance: what evidence will satisfy most enterprise procurement teams in EU and APAC?
3) Laura/Hiroshi — can you confirm whether your teams can attend a 45‑minute kickoff the week of Apr 19 and if you have a local technical lead to include?

I propose a shared meeting and a short mutual action plan (MAP) that includes evidence exchange and a 4‑week pilot.

Thanks,
Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz

Quick answers from the EU side: ClearSky can own introductions to local cloud providers in FR/DE/UK (we have existing reseller relationships) and we have a certified technical lead who has run on‑prem inference pilots for two banks. We can attend the week of Apr 19; preferably Apr 21 afternoon CEST.

For procurement, EU customers will want:
- SOC2 or equivalent assurance statements (Type II preferred)
- A clear data flow diagram that shows where customer data is processed and stored
- Contract language about data export controls and subprocessor lists

We can provide a sample SOW and a short partner capabilities slide deck ahead of the kickoff.

Suggested next step: a 45‑minute kickoff where we review the matrix, agree MAP owners, and identify required artifacts. I can share a sample SOW and a short checklist — will upload in next email.

A few APAC notes from our side:
- Japan and Australia customers often require data residency or at least a clear contractual commitment that logs and PII remain in region.
- For regulated customers we have deployed vendor code in customer VPCs and used KMS integration for key separation.
- We can bring a technical lead for the kickoff; Apr 20–22 JST works for our team.

We also request a short technical evidence pack from Redwood: DFD (data flow diagram), list of supported KMS providers, and any whitepaper that explains Redwood Private on‑prem package.

We look forward to the MAP and can propose a pilot customer (midmarket retail) that is interested in edge inference and data residency.

Regards,
